accelBuiltinBody:
1. What this is
This is the separate agreement for the **built-in acceleration channel**. The built-in channel is deployed and maintained by this application's developer, to provide a faster path when downloading GitHub release assets, Actions run logs and build artifacts.

**It is a different document from the Application Privacy Commitment**: that one binds the application only, not this channel.

2. We promise: no data is stored
1. The channel **keeps no copy** of the files you download; data is released from memory once forwarding completes — nothing is written to disk, archived or retained.
2. The channel **records nothing that identifies you**: not your GitHub account, token, repository names or file contents.
3. The channel **never receives your GitHub access token**: the application first exchanges the authenticated URL, locally on your device, for a GitHub-issued temporary signed address valid for about 30 minutes and for a single file only, and hands that signed address to the channel. The channel sees only that temporary credential and cannot use it to reach your account or other files.
4. The channel **sets no cookies**, **uses no third-party analytics or advertising components**, and **plays no part in your sign-in**.

3. We do **not** guarantee availability
1. The channel may be **interrupted, slowed or unavailable** due to maintenance, rate limiting, bandwidth limits, network failures or force majeure. This application makes **no availability commitment** whatsoever.
2. The channel **may lack some proxy endpoints**: certain kinds of resources may not be retrievable through it. In that case the application falls back automatically to the official GitHub address directly — functionality is unaffected (it merely becomes slower).
3. Should problems occur, you can **turn acceleration off**, or switch to a **custom channel**.

4. Risks you should know
1. That ~30-minute signed address is itself a temporary credential "for that file only". Within its validity the channel **is technically able to fetch that file itself**, and may log the address. Please judge on that basis whether you accept it.
2. The whole transfer uses HTTPS (TLS), but encryption only guarantees that no third party can eavesdrop in transit; it does not change the facts above.

5. Content integrity
After download completes, the application compares the SHA-256 digest provided by GitHub; a mismatch marks the file as failed and it is **not** exported to your chosen folder. When no digest is available, it is honestly labelled "not verified".

6. Applicability and termination
1. This agreement takes effect on the day you accept it. You may turn the master switch off at any time to stop using this channel.
2. Any material change to the text will raise the consent version and require your confirmation again; it never takes effect silently.
accelThirdPartyBody:
1. What this is
This is the notice for a **custom acceleration channel**. The channel address is **added by you**, and its operator is **not** the developer of this application.

**This application ships no acceleration channel of its own and provides no proxy service.** If you add no channel, there is no acceleration.

2. Prefix-style proxies only
This application **supports prefix-style proxies only** (for example the GHproxy project): the complete original link is appended after the proxy prefix, as in `https://your-proxy/original-full-link`.

Proxy forms that need to rewrite request headers, rewrite URL paths, or implement their own authentication logic are **not supported**.

3. Capabilities may be incomplete (please be aware)
1. A prefix-style proxy may **lack some endpoints**, so certain kinds of resources may be unavailable through it.
2. If some features misbehave or network loading fails, this application will **not silently fall back to a direct connection** — it reports the failure as it is. That is how you can tell whether traffic really went through the channel. If you want a direct connection, turn the main switch off.
3. This application **does not guarantee** the availability, speed, or completeness of any custom channel.

4. Responsibility
1. The channel's operator, availability, bandwidth, stability, content integrity, and security are **the third party's responsibility**; this application gives no warranty of any kind.
2. Once enabled, some download requests (including the target download address) will be sent to that third-party server. Please satisfy yourself that you trust that provider, and assess the privacy, data, and compliance risks on your own.
3. This application compares the SHA-256 digest provided by GitHub where one is available; but if the third party returns a file that does not match, or the resource has no digest, this application **cannot guarantee it was not substituted**.
4. This application accepts no liability for download failures, data corruption, tampered content, privacy leaks, extra charges, or any direct or indirect loss arising from use of that third-party service.
5. You are responsible for checking and complying with the laws and internal policies of your country/region and organisation regarding network access and data transmission.

5. Token protection
To avoid handing your GitHub token to a third party, this application first exchanges it **locally on your device** for a temporary signed address valid for about 30 minutes and suitable for a single file, and hands that address to the channel. Within that validity window the channel could technically take that file itself, and may log the address.

6. Scope and termination
1. This notice is shown from the moment you tick to accept. You may remove the channel or turn the main switch off at any time to stop using it.
2. From the moment you stop, this application sends no further requests to that channel.

fileTooLargeTitle: File too large for the built-in preview
fileTooLargeBody:
GitHub's Contents API returns no content for files over 1 MB, so the built-in preview cannot fetch the bytes.
You can switch to opening it via a raw link (faster, but it goes through the current acceleration channel), or adjust the acceleration method in Settings.
accelServiceBody:
Acceleration channels are a **network service provided by this application**, not merely a technical forwarding mechanism.

· **Availability is not guaranteed**: the service may be interrupted by maintenance, rate limiting, network failure, or force majeure; this application accepts no liability for that.
· **Absence of data collection is not guaranteed**: the service **may** record access logs, IP addresses, User-Agent strings, and similar information while running. This application makes no promise in this regard.
· **Off by default**: acceleration is disabled by default; you must enable it explicitly in Settings.
· **No repeated prompt after enabling**: enabling acceleration in Settings counts as acceptance of the above; no further dialog will appear.
· **Prompted again when you add a custom channel**: because a custom channel is specified by you, its operator and behaviour are the responsibility of that third party.
accelPrefixOnlyBody:
A custom channel **allows prefix-style proxies only** (such as the GHproxy project): the complete original link is appended after the proxy prefix.

Proxy forms that need to rewrite request headers, rewrite URL paths, or implement their own authentication logic are not supported.

**Note**: a prefix-style proxy may **lack some proxy endpoints**. If some feature misbehaves or network loading fails, you can try switching to the built-in proxy or turning acceleration off.
accelLangNote: The **Chinese text is the original wording** of this note. Translations are provided for understanding only; where a translation differs, **the Chinese original prevails**.

fileTooLargeBodyPrivate:
GitHub's Contents API returns no content for files over 1 MB, so the built-in preview cannot fetch the bytes.
This is a private repository: acceleration does not apply to it (a private repo's raw requires a token to fetch, and handing it to a proxy means handing over the token), so enabling acceleration will not change how this is fetched.
You can switch to opening it via a raw link, or download it to view.
accelNoChannelBody: This application ships no channel and runs no proxy. To accelerate, add a prefix-style proxy address of your own; otherwise everything stays on a direct connection.
accelSelfProvided: Channels are yours to provide: this app bundles none, recommends none, and hosts none.
webAccelNoticeBody:
The browser build has no persistent built-in acceleration channel, so downloads such as Release assets go direct by default.

You can use the app perfectly well without configuring anything — only the download speed depends on your network and on how reachable GitHub is for you.

To accelerate, add a channel yourself under Settings → Network → Acceleration; you can turn it off at any time.
webInstallDialogBody:
Add this app to your desktop / home screen so it later opens on its own, like a normal app.

Selecting “Confirm” opens the browser's install prompt.
webInstallIosBody:
iOS browsers do not support one-tap adding (a platform limitation, not an app issue).

Tap the “Share” button at the bottom, then choose “Add to Home Screen”.
webInstallChromiumBody:
The browser did not offer one-tap installation this time (it may already be installed, or this page does not meet the install criteria yet).

You can still choose “Install app” or “Add to Home Screen” from the browser menu.
